rv.q: Part Two finds its footing and doesn’t take one wrong step: the humour working brilliantly in occasional flecks, the drama leading with emotion, thought and the everyday tragedy of marital disappointment.

It is a deftly clever adaptation. More than 800 pages boiled down into some six hours and two plays, a whole world unfolding on a virtually bare stage, and an entire community brought vividly into view as they grapple with the twists and turns of lives that make it hard to fulfil their hopes and dreams.
